summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and advanced HIV (CD4 39, high viral load) was admitted for progressive right leg swelling following placement of a right femoral dialysis catheter. Ultrasound showed no deep vein thrombosis in the leg, but CT revealed the catheter occupying the right external iliac vein, limiting clot assessment. Given clinical suspicion, she was treated for presumed catheter-related deep vein thrombosis with heparin followed by warfarin, with complete resolution of edema. During admission, she developed conjunctivitis with periorbital swelling; given her history of herpes zoster ophthalmicus, she was treated with valacyclovir and topical antibiotics, with marked improvement. Chest discomfort was attributed to esophagitis and resolved with fluconazole. She continued her HAART regimen and dialysis, with dose adjustment of cinacalcet. She was discharged home on warfarin, valacyclovir, and eye ointment, with close outpatient monitoring.
problems: Other complications due to renal dialysis device, implant, and graft
Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of unspecified deep vessels of lower extremity
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Kidney dialysis as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
